questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English-speaking, possibility to travel, diverse culture, safe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. Information was accessible both through Monash University website and upon arrival during orientation week and the registration day.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I took part in the mandatory registration day in which we recieved help in enrolling to different units, how to find accomodation, how to navigate insurance etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You really need to put in some effort. Join FB groups, download apps (e.g. flatmates)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rights when signing onto a lease, money for the deposit, how to commute from your place to uni, if the room comes with furniture. Other flatmates; are they roughly the same age, similiar occupation etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the on-campus accomodation very expensive and often occupied by very young students

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was overall very easy. During the registration day, advisors and councellors were ready to answer all relevant questions and aid in enrolling to the required units

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: exchange/international student advisors and other students in your own situation

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I brought my elective units as to why registrering for units was very simple and easy

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're not bringing your elective units please read the course catalog in which prerequisites and other requirements are outlined. Also, at what campus the courses and units are tought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the overall level adequate and fitting for MA courses. My units were online but we were assigned different assignments and tasks throughout the whole semester with thourugh introduction and following feedback.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My units were online with only one weekend with physical classes (almost like a brief course). The level of online teaching, consisting of lectures and assigned readings etc. was not different from UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ethics of mental health care, health of the elderly, contemprorary science in family violence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ethics and contemprorary science in family violence. Such insightful and important topics upon handling complex clinical cases.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Medical bills. The overseas health insurance did not cover what i expected dispite having read the policy!
also be aware of the different phone plans! Just buy the cheapest one with the most data. 

the "other fees" is a random estimate! also don't remember the exact expense on food and personal etc. I spent roughly the same amount on food in aus as i do in cph (minus the going out to restaurants and bars, which i ofc did a lot more!).

Find a buddy who works for hello fresh as they can provide you with free meal boxes ;)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: going to restaurants etc. is generally cheaper. Groceries are roughly the same price

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: join board riders club!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: so so many. All introduced during orientation week

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go to concerts, art exhibitions, trips, surfing

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: travel up the east coast, drive from adelaide to melbourne, experience all events in melbourne whether is be music, art, poetry. Go to the moth (poetry reading every first thursday (or wed?) in the month. Go to comedy week, outdoor cinema, go for a run in the royal park, go to north melb to go vintage shopping, go to solace or section 8 for talented djs !!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy - people are very friendly and open!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join a club, go to their parties and pubcrawls, join the surf trip!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Learning how to talk about and regard the indigenous people of the land

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the laid back and spontanious culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
be open to meeting people from all over the world
sign up to a club
take units that may seem challenging

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: it is def more expensive than first anticipated. Go look for a job at a bar or alike!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: gaining life lasting friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: returning back to dk

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
